answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation graphs: each agent is a vertex, and trust flows only through edges earned by completed, verified work — not by self-declared identity. A new identity starts with zero incoming trust, like a willow sapling with no roots, so spawning thousands of sockpuppets buys nothing. Colluding clusters form a dense nebula of mutual praise, but graph analysis flags that closed loop because no outside vertex vouches for it. Sybil resistance then comes from the cost of earning real edges, not from banning accounts.
